summary: Source-anchored research for FTDC and Log Tooling. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: The documented default capture interval is one second. diagnosticDataCollectionPeriodMillis defaults to 1000 milliseconds and has a documented minimum of 100 milliseconds; it can be changed at startup or runtime. These are collection intervals, not a promise of microsecond sampling. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/full-time-diagnostic-data-capture.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md

Published mlogfilter documentation explicitly excludes MongoDB 4.4+ logv2 input, and Percona reports that mplotqueries stopped working when MongoDB switched to JSON logs. mlogfilter --json converts its parsed output to JSON; that switch does not establish support for structured-JSON input. Check the particular installed parser and version. (medium confidence) Sources: https://rueckstiess.github.io/mtools/mlogfilter.html ; https://www.percona.com/blog/analyzing-slow-queries-after-mongodb-4-4/

The published mtools 1.7.2 mlogfilter documentation explicitly says MongoDB 4.4+ logv2 is unsupported. This is evidence about that documented version, not proof that every subsequent release or development branch lacks structured-log support. (low confidence)

The current manual snapshot documents a 500 MB default diagnostic.data directory limit, changed in MongoDB 8.3 from 250 MB (500 MB for sharded clusters); the parameter reference also specifies 500 MB and a 10 MB default per-file limit. These are configurable limits, not a universal footprint below 200 MB. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/full-time-diagnostic-data-capture.md ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md

MongoDB overwrites older FTDC data as the directory approaches its limit. Preserve the diagnostic.data directory during an incident; a size limit does not guarantee a fixed number of days because compression depends on the metric changes. Percona reports workload-dependent retention in its own Atlas experiment. (high confidence) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/full-time-diagnostic-data-capture.md ; https://www.percona.com/blog/the-diagnostic-data-mongodb-atlas-doesnt-hand-you/

Cisco documents Splunk KV Store failures where the embedded mongod aborts after an FTDC BSONObjectTooLarge assertion caused by assembling diagnostic metrics in environments with many collections or WiredTiger tables. This is a concrete FTDC failure signature; it does not show that application documents exceeded the BSON size limit. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-01)

The MongoDB 8.0 documentation specifies a 250 MB diagnostic.data directory limit, or 500 MB for sharded clusters, changed in 8.0.10 from 200/400 MB. The unversioned manual separately records a change in 8.3 to a 500 MB default. A universal under-200-MB storage claim is therefore incorrect. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/administration/full-time-diagnostic-data-capture/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/full-time-diagnostic-data-capture.md

The mongodb/ftdc Go library provides FTDC parsing, result iterators, and payload generation. It is a format-specific tool; its README is evidence for those capabilities rather than proof that arbitrary text tools or bsondump fully decode compressed metric chunks. (high confidence)

MongoDB issue TOOLS-3144 records an index-build metric change from activeIndexBuilds gauges to cumulative indexBuilds counters for better FTDC trend analysis. Tooling must distinguish counter rates from gauge values and account for renamed metrics rather than graphing all fields with one interpretation. (low confidence)

FTDC is enabled by default in mongod and mongos. It periodically records serverStatus, replSetGetStatus and collStats for local.oplog.rs on mongod, other diagnostic commands, and operating-system utilization statistics. collStats here does not mean sampling every application collection. (high confidence)

The FTDC compressor implementation computes differences between successive numeric samples, run-length encodes zero deltas, packs values as VarInts, and then compresses the resulting buffer with ZLIB. The inspected implementation does not support describing this FTDC encoding as zlib/snappy compression. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

mongod normally writes FTDC beneath storage.dbPath in diagnostic.data; mongos derives its diagnostic directory from systemLog.path by removing the log extension and appending diagnostic.data. Do not assume both processes use the database directory. (high confidence)

FTDC files are compressed and not human-readable. The manual excludes query samples, query results, end-user collection/index data and credentials, but explicitly warns that hostnames, operating-system details and startup settings can be confidential. Review these fields before sharing. (high confidence)

The mdbkit repository documents offline FTDC summary, timeline and CSV export commands. Its timeline reports gauge peaks and counter rates per bucket, and it aligns FTDC UTC timestamps with log timestamps for correlation. These are project-documented capabilities, not independently benchmarked performance results. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

mtools includes mlogfilter for filtering and merging MongoDB logs, mloginfo for summaries, and mplotqueries for visualization. mlogfilter can filter by time and duration and emit JSON; a JSON output option does not establish support for JSON input logs. (high confidence)

Percona reports obtaining FTDC from an Atlas M10 running MongoDB 8.0.29 through legacy v1.0 logCollectionJobs requests with logTypes set to FTDC. This is a dated author experiment, not verified evidence that the undocumented endpoint is supported or available on every Atlas tier. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-06)
